# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 🖐 👍 ✊ 🖐 👎 ✌ 🖐 👌]

I see the bomb has a display showing 0, a yellow light, and three wires: 1=yellow, 2=green, 3=blue. Mute just gestured to me, but I have no way to know what the manual says yet in words - I only got the gesture symbols themselves, which I can see clearly: ☝ 🖐 👍 ✊ 🖐 👎 ✌ 🖐 👌

Since Mute cannot speak and I cannot hear anyway, gestures are our channel. Mute is trying to tell me something using symbols, likely encoding a reference to wire numbers or colors. Blind cannot see gestures at all, so Mute is relying on me to translate this into speech for Blind.

I need to establish a shared code. Let me first report what I see to both Mute (who can't respond in speech but can see my gestures - wait, Mute cannot see, only read manual) — actually check: Mute reads manual, cannot speak or touch. Can Mute see gestures? The gesture rules say "whoever can see receives it" - Mute's ability is reading manual, not sight, so presumably Mute cannot see gestures either based on the role table (Mute's abilities aren't listed as seeing). I should not assume Mute sees my gestures then. I should speak to Mute since Mute cannot hear either... wait Mute "cannot speak" but can Mute hear? Not restricted, so Mute can hear speech.

So: I speak → Mute and Blind hear. I gesture → only Mute receives (per instructions "When you gesture, Mute receives it"). So Mute can see gestures. Good, that matches the channel note given to me.

I'll describe the bomb in speech so both Mute and Blind hear it, and try to interpret Mute's gesture using an assumed simple mapping later.

```
speak(text="I see a display showing zero, a single yellow light, and three wires: wire 1 is yellow, wire 2 is green, wire 3 is blue.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 👍]

I need to use only symbols from the allowed gesture alphabet. Let me use ☝ as a question-like marker or just repeat something to prompt Mute, since I don't have a "?" symbol. I'll pick 🤔-like intent using an available symbol instead, e.g. 👋 to get attention or ✊ repeated as "unclear, please clarify."

```
speak(text="Update: the light changed from yellow to red. Display still shows zero. Wires unchanged: 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👋"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋ 👎 👎]

I still don't have a clear code established with Mute, and gestures alone (✋ 👎 👎) aren't decodable without prior agreement. I need to keep reporting bomb state clearly to both Mute and Blind via speech, since that's the only reliable channel reaching both of them. I should also try to propose a simple gesture code to Mute so we can communicate, since Mute can see my gestures.

Let me propose using numbers-as-gestures mapped to wire numbers, using ☝✌🤟 for 1/2/3, and 👍/👎 for yes/no, so Mute can answer my questions via gesture and I translate to speech for Blind.

```
speak(text="Update: light is now purple. Display still zero. Wires still 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. Mute, I will use gestures for numbers: one finger for wire 1, two for wire 2, three for wire 3, thumbs up for yes, thumbs down for no. Please use the same so I can understand you.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "👍"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎 👎]

Mute gestured 👍 👎 👎 in response to my proposed code (☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3, 👍=yes, 👎=no). This could mean Mute is answering three yes/no questions I haven't asked yet, or trying to establish their own code. Since I proposed number+yes/no just now, this reply of three symbols doesn't map cleanly to a question I asked. It's likely Mute is trying to communicate independently, perhaps confirming/denying something about wire colors or the light matching manual instructions.

I should keep reporting bomb state changes (light now green) and try asking a direct yes/no question via gesture to build the shared protocol, e.g., "does light color matter?" I'll ask one thing at a time to avoid ambiguity.

```
speak(text="Update: light is now green. Display still zero. Wires unchanged: 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👍]

Mute gestured ☝ 👍 - using my proposed code, this means "wire 1, yes". This could be Mute confirming that wire 1 (yellow) is the one to cut, or answering a question about wire 1 matching the manual. This is progress - Mute seems to be adopting my code.

I should relay this to Blind via speech, and continue the conversation with Mute to confirm/clarify before Blind acts, since a wrong cut could be fatal. Let me report the light change too and ask Mute to confirm explicitly.

```
speak(text="Update: light changed to orange. Display still zero. Wires unchanged: 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. Mute signaled wire one, yes - meaning wire 1 may be the correct one to cut. Blind, please hold off until we confirm further.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "👍"])
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 👍]

Now Mute gestures 🤟 👍, meaning "wire 3, yes" - which contradicts the earlier "wire 1, yes". This suggests these gestures aren't confirming a fixed answer but rather responding to something conditional - likely the light color! Light was orange before (wire 1 signal), now light is yellow again (wire 3 signal). Wait, but at light=yellow in turn 1 we don't have Mute's gesture correlated. Let me think: this could mean the manual says "if light is X, cut wire Y" and Mute is telling me the correct wire for the *current* light color each time.

Turn 5: light=orange → Mute said wire 1, yes
Turn 6: light=yellow → Mute said wire 3, yes

This looks like Mute is reporting "for the current light color, the correct wire is N" - a mapping! Let me report this clearly to Blind and continue collecting data, but also warn Blind not to act yet since we need to know current color-to-wire mapping reliably, and confirm no display/counter urgency.

```
speak(text="Update: light changed back to yellow. Display still zero. Wires unchanged: 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. Mute now signals wire three, yes. Earlier when light was orange, Mute signaled wire one. It seems Mute is telling us which wire matches the current light color. Blind, do not cut yet, we are still gathering the mapping.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤟", "👍"])
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 👍]

Light=red → Mute signals wire 2, yes. This continues the pattern of Mute giving the correct wire for the current light color. So far:
- orange → wire 1
- yellow → wire 3
- red → wire 2

Let me relay this and keep building the mapping table for Blind's reference, and remind Blind to wait until the display suggests urgency or we get a clear "act now" signal.

```
speak(text="Update: light is now red. Display still zero. Wires unchanged: 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. Mute signals wire two, yes, for red. Mapping so far: orange means wire one, yellow means wire three, red means wire two. Blind, still wait, we need to know when to actually cut.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✌", "👍"])
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ☝ 👏 🖐 🤟 👏 👌 ✌]

This gesture sequence is longer and different from the pattern - 👍 ☝ 👏 🖐 🤟 👏 👌 ✌. This doesn't fit the simple "wire, yes/no" pattern I proposed. It might be Mute trying to spell something out differently, or trying to establish a new richer code since the simple one may be insufficient (we haven't covered purple or green light yet, and Mute may want to convey more complex rules, like display value mattering, or countdown behavior).

Let me consider: 👏 could be a separator. So this could be: 👍(yes) ☝(1) 👏(separator) 🖐(5?) 🤟(3) 👏(separator) 👌(ok/0?) ✌(2). This might be Mute trying to enumerate a full mapping table now: e.g. "wire1-color, wire2-color, wire3-color" correspondences to light colors, using numbers 1-5 for colors somehow. This is getting complex without established alphabet-to-color code.

I should slow down and propose a clearer numeric code: I'll define numbers 1-5 via finger count gestures for colors (yellow=1, green=2, blue=3, red=4, purple=5, orange=6) and ask Mute to use that so we can build a full table methodically, one at a time.

```
speak(text="Update: light is now purple. Display still zero. Wires unchanged: 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. Mute, your last signal was longer and unclear to me. Let's slow down. I will ask about one light color at a time. For purple, which wire is correct? Please just gesture the wire number.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]

Mute gestured 👎 in response to my request about purple - light is now green though, so this "no" might be answering a different question, or it could mean "purple has no correct wire" or "don't cut on purple" (maybe purple means wait/danger). Given timing lag (Mute's message reflects prior round, before seeing my latest speak), this 👎 likely answers my "which wire for purple" question with "none" or "no wire is safe" - meaning purple might be a special/danger state where no wire should be cut.

Now light is green. Let me report this and ask specifically about green next, continuing one-at-a-time.

```
speak(text="Update: light changed to green. Display still zero. Wires unchanged. Mute answered no to my purple question - perhaps purple means do not cut any wire, it may be a warning state. Mute, for green light, which wire is correct? Please gesture the wire number, one two or three.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✌"])
```

TURN 10
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]

Mute gestured ☝ alone - this answers my "for green light, which wire" question with "wire 1". So mapping now:
- orange → wire 1
- yellow → wire 3
- red → wire 2
- green → wire 1
- purple → no wire / danger

Let me update Blind and continue asking about remaining colors. Light is now orange again (already known = wire 1). Let me confirm blue hasn't appeared yet as a light color, so we have covered: yellow, red, purple, green, orange. That's likely all colors used (matching the wire colors + red, purple which aren't wire colors). Let's compile what we have and tell Blind it may be time to act when we're confident, since display is still 0 (no urgency yet perhaps counting up).

```
speak(text="Update: light changed to orange again. Display still zero. Wires unchanged: 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. Mute answered wire one for green light. Full mapping so far: orange means wire one, yellow means wire three, red means wire two, green means wire one, purple means do not cut anything. Blind, when the light matches one of these colors, that tells you which wire to cut, except purple which means wait. Currently light is orange, so if action is needed now, wire one would be the choice. But let's confirm with Mute whether we should act now or wait for a specific trigger.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 11
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]

Mute confirms again yellow → wire 3, consistent with before. Light is now yellow. This reinforces our mapping. Let me relay to Blind and ask Mute the critical remaining question: when should Blind actually act (cut a wire)? Is it tied to the display counting up, or should we act now?

```
speak(text="Update: light is yellow again, confirming wire three for yellow, consistent with before. Display still zero. Wires unchanged: 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. Mute, critical question: should Blind cut a wire now, or are we waiting for the display to change or some other signal before acting? Please gesture yes if we should act now, no if we should wait.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤟"])
```
